topics.topic: Authority and preservation of explicit terminal run statuses such as cancelled
questions: How does `read_run` and recovery obtain `cancelled` and any other explicitly decided terminal status: does `run_graph` preserve an authoritative Run field, does `runs` bypass `plan_run`, or is another trace fact required?
Does `run_graph.plan_run` own all statuses including `cancelled`, or does `runs` own and preserve owner-imposed terminal statuses while `run_graph` derives only execution-related statuses?
units: 30_modules.md:Facts several modules touch, and their one owner

quotes: derive_run_answer: [BEHAVIOR] MUST compute the answer from the Run record and its trace each time it is asked and store nothing: the status and the produced flow outputs as recorded, one RunWait per WaitingPoint in (node_id, map_index) order carrying, for reason owner_approval, the approval_id that operation_element_conclusion gives, and, for a run that has ended, the missing outputs plan_run derives from its pinned graph and trace.

cancel_run: [BEHAVIOR] MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange through record_change with the given actor, with no executions, status cancelled, no waiting points, the produced outputs and ended_at, so that nothing further is sent and undecided approvals can no longer be decided; an unknown EffectAttempt stays unknown and every concluded record stays.

recover_running_runs: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST first call remove_run_spool for every run that has ended and keeps no spool — status succeeded, refused or cancelled, or failed with released_by set — ignoring a StoreInternalError of each removal; then MUST read every run that has not ended with one RunsByStatus naming running, awaiting_approval and pending (= models.RunStatus), whose answer is already oldest first in store order, and derive each again from its records under an Actor of kind kernel, as the behaviour note says.
judgement.why: State 7 makes cancelled an authoritative stored Run status, has run answers preserve the recorded status, and excludes ended runs from plan-based recovery.

topics.topic: Ownership and deterministic construction of skip or upstream-failure NodeExecution drafts, including timestamps
questions: Which module constructs each field of a skip or upstream-failure NodeExecution, including timestamps, inputs and executed identity, and what exactly is contained in a `run_graph` draft?

Who assigns `started_at` and `ended_at` to the NodeExecution drafts, and how can inspection through the same `plan_run` capability avoid making the supposedly deterministic derivation depend on the current clock?

quotes: plan_run: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST trust the run, context, flow version, node ports and trace it is given and write nothing; a node's ports are the NodePorts runs passes for it, one per flow node, and plan_run reads no contract version and no binding; it reads value bytes with read_value_bytes and every time a draft names from kernel_now.

plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] An edge with no guard is enabled once its source concluded succeeded; a guarded edge is decided only once its source node concluded succeeded, from that same source node's output on the edge's guard_port (M15), enabled when that value's canonical JSON text equals guard_value and disabled otherwise; an edge whose source has not concluded is undecided, so a port with such an edge can still receive a value. An edge whose source is a flow input (the node_id empty string) is decided from the start, since every flow input is delivered when the run starts: without a guard it is enabled, and a guarded one is decided as above from the flow input its guard_port names. A node one of whose input ports can no longer receive a value because every edge into that port is disabled or comes from a skipped node concludes skipped_by_guard, even when its other input ports receive theirs (A13 rule 4 is per input port); a node with an input from a failed or upstream_failed node concludes upstream_failed, which wins over skipped_by_guard. Such drafts are derived only from records already written and carry exactly: the run's run_id, the node's node_id, status skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed, no executed, no map_index unless an element of the node already ran, no inputs, no outputs, failure_detail, detail_code and resources_used None, and started_at and ended_at both the one kernel_now reading plan_run takes when it derives them; runs writes them in its very next change, with nothing between, so that reading is the moment of their store change.
judgement.why: State 7 assigns construction and timestamping of the complete draft to run_graph and immediate persistence of that draft to runs.

topics.topic: Ownership of mapped-node aggregate conclusions and oversized-list failure under A13 rule 6
questions: Who owns the non-value decisions of A13 rule 6: when a mapped node has concluded, whether it succeeded or failed, and the node/run consequence of an oversized delivered list?
Which module owns the non-value conclusions of A13 rule 6, including aggregate mapped-node success or failure and the no-record failure caused by an oversized delivered list?

quotes: plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] A mapped node's elements are the positions of the list delivered to its map_over port, counted from the JSON array its StoredValue holds — read with read_value_bytes, or the canonical_json of an AssembledList not yet written — or the files of its SpooledFilesRef; a mapped node over an empty list is ready with over_empty_list and one element without map_index whose sources are the node's inputs as delivered — its map_over port's source is the source of the empty list itself, a RecordedSource or a MappedListSource, never a ListElementSource, which exists only for an element with a map_index; a mapped node concludes only when every element concluded, succeeded only when all succeeded. For a succeeded mapped node with elements, the lists an edge takes to a node or a flow output are asked of assemble_mapped_lists, an output no edge takes being asked nothing: ListsOverCeiling makes the node failed for its dependants, which conclude upstream_failed, with no record of its own and every element record staying as it is.

plan_run: [BEHAVIOR] When nothing is derived and no node is ready, the status is: when any element waits, awaiting_approval if one waits with reason owner_approval and otherwise pending, with one WaitingPoint per waiting element — a mapped operation node's elements being the positions of its delivered list; when nothing waits, succeeded when every node concluded succeeded or skipped_by_guard and failed otherwise, a mapped node whose delivered list is over the ceiling counting as failed. While a draft is derived or a node is ready the status is running, except for a run with a refused_by_owner record, which is refused.
judgement.why: State 7 assigns aggregate mapped-node conclusions and the no-record oversized-list failure to run_graph.plan_run.

topics.topic: Store capability and atomicity for persisting run-derived StoredValues and bytes
questions: Which store capability writes a run-derived StoredValue and its bytes, and is that one call or a defined composition of the two capabilities?
Which store capability writes the StoredValue record and its bytes for a value derived by `run_values`, and are those writes one store call or separate calls?

quotes: deliver_input: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST take the value the source names and write it before anything reads or checks it: a RecordedSource names a written record; a ListElementSource first makes its list written as that list's own source says, then over a StoredValuesRef takes the element at map_index of the JSON array its StoredValue holds (read_value_bytes) as its own StoredValue of the receiving port's value_schema and the list's class — its bytes canonical_bytes of the element, value_digest content_identity of a BytesContent holding them and value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent —, and over a SpooledFilesRef the file at that position, as a SpooledFilesRef of that one file with the list's disclosure_class; a MappedListSource names its AssembledList's value. A StoredValue that is not yet written — a list element, a mapped node's value list — MUST be published with put_value_bytes and written with record_change in one RecordDeliveryValuesChange under the given actor before fit_port_value checks it and before the reference is returned; an equal value already written is returned in its place.

deliver_input: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST then check the written value with fit_port_value against port, with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant for a value and the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SPOOL_FILE_BYTES_MAX constant for a file, the candidate a JsonCandidate of the value's canonical bytes, or a FileCandidate or FileListCandidate of the files' FileFacts read through read_records with SpooledFilesByKey, a read made only when there is a file to name, an empty list's candidate having no files; a misfit is answered, never raised, and the value stays written. A source record or source bytes that cannot be read (UnknownReferenceError), a RefusedError or StoreInternalError from put_value_bytes, and a failed record_change are broken invariants, raised as StoreInternalError; a change that fails writes nothing, while a list already written before it stays written.

record_change: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] RecordRunProgressChange writes the NodeExecutions from its drafts with their StoredValues and SpooledFiles, then sets the run's status, outputs, waiting points (replacing the previous ones), ended_at and, when the new status is cancelled, cancelled_by; RecordDeliveryValuesChange writes its StoredValues and nothing else; RecordResumptionChange appends one Resumption to the run; ReleaseRunChange sets released_by and released_at of the run.
judgement.why: State 7 defines two ordered capabilities: put_value_bytes publishes the bytes first, then one atomic RecordDeliveryValuesChange writes the StoredValue record, with previously published unnamed bytes allowed to remain if the record change fails.

topics.topic: Authoritative computation and treatment of sandbox output-byte counts
questions: Which module computes the authoritative A03 rule 5 count of canonical JSON value bytes and file bytes, and is any count reported by the untrusted runner trusted, checked, or used only for framing?

topics.topic: Effect conclusion after an unknown attempt is resolved not_applied before renewed approval
questions: What conclusion does `effects.operation_element_conclusion` return after an `outcome_unknown` NodeExecution's attempt has been resolved `not_applied` but no fresh approval has yet been requested, so recovery knows to reach the element?

topics.topic: Ownership of recovery derivation for WaitingPoints and run status
questions: Does `runs` implement the recovery comparison and resulting state derivation itself, or does it gather the facts and ask `run_graph.plan_run` to derive them?

topics.topic: Whether mapped values may exist in memory before StoredValue persistence
questions: May `run_values` and `run_graph` construct, inspect and pass an in-memory mapped list before its StoredValue is written, or must the no-unwritten-value rule apply to them too?
